recorded_from: run 42029618358, the full dispatch of 92a1647f on 2026-11-05, and run 42079970039, the full dispatch of 031f946e on 2026-11-05; Test_normalization_forced and the adapter hooks that back it were added by #1144 before a dispatch ran them, and the test that asks it PASSes on a dedicated server by returning at Test.overlay_supported

why.net/grug/minecraft/core/GrugTestRunner$4: The seam that forwards a test's forced autosave and its forced-normalization hooks to the adapter. The autosave hook is reached only by a test whose name asks for a save tick, and that test reads the save indicator a client draws. The normalization hooks are reached only for a marked test on a client: a dedicated server runs hook_forced_normalization-Test.grug and PASSes by returning at Test.overlay_supported, and the runner's GrugForcedNormalization.appliesTo is false there, so a server never calls them. The dispatch's check counts a test a dedicated server ran as reaching what that test reaches on the client, so it offers these entries for removal; they stay because the server's run of the test returns at Test.overlay_supported and never reaches them.
why.net/grug/minecraft/core/ModLoaderAdapter: The test hooks an adapter keeps the no-op default for: the forced-normalization hook (canForceNormalizationForTest, forceNormalizationForTest, restoreNormalizationAfterTest, normalizationEnabledForTest) runs only for a marked test on a client. A dedicated server runs the coverage test that would ask it, but it PASSes by returning at Test.overlay_supported, and the runner's GrugForcedNormalization.appliesTo is false on a server, so it never calls the hooks there. 1.20.6 keeps all four defaults on its client too, because its item draw uses its own shader path. The dispatch's check counts a test a dedicated server ran as reaching what that test reaches on the client, so it offers these entries for removal; they stay because the server's run of the test returns at Test.overlay_supported and never reaches them.
why.net/grug/minecraft/forge/ForgeAdapter: The game directory the capture path writes under and the crack overlay a client draws, both reached only by tests that read a frame; requestAutosaveForTest saves through the client's integrated server, which a dedicated server does not have. The boot's own game directory read is in the boot segment, which the map leaves out.
why.net/grug/minecraft/forge125/Grug125Adapt: The game directory and its 1.2.5 name, which the client's captures write under; a dedicated server captures nothing, and the boot's read is in the boot segment the map leaves out.
why.net/grug/minecraft/forge125/Grug125Clien: The client half of the 1.2.5 loader: the mining crack overlay, the screen only a client opens, and the forced-normalization hook a marked test asks for on a client. The runner's GrugForcedNormalization.appliesTo answers false on a dedicated server, and the coverage test that reads the forced state returns at Test.overlay_supported there, so no server reaches them. The dispatch's check counts a test a dedicated server ran as reaching what that test reaches on the client, so it offers these entries for removal; they stay because the server's run of the test returns at Test.overlay_supported and never reaches them.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugBlockFaces: Reads a block's model JSON from the mods directory and follows its parent chain, once per process when the loaders register their blocks. A dedicated server does that read too, through GrugBlocks' call to GrugBlockModels.resolveFaceTextures, and the map attributes it to whichever test's segment it happens to land in: run 42029618358 needed no entry for these methods because its segment was one that loader's server ran. Only the client re-reads a model on a hot reload, and the two tests that do, hot_reload_texture and hot_reload_item_texture, capture a frame, so no dedicated server runs them. 1.20.6 leaves the reading to the game's own model baking.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugFaceTextures: The per-face keys a built-in model parent supplies and the texture each face key resolves to, reached through GrugBlockFaces at the same one-time block registration. A dedicated server resolves them there too, and which test's segment the map attributes that read to is what varies, as the GrugBlockFaces reason says.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugModFileState: Hot reload swaps a changed file aside on the client's watcher; a dedicated server reloads no mod file.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugModels: Reads a mod's model files, which a client does to draw a block or an item; a dedicated server draws nothing and reads none of them.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugModels$Cache: A model built for drawing and kept for the next frame that needs it; a dedicated server builds no model.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugModels$Defec: The record of a model file that could not be read, which only a client's model load produces.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugModsWatcher: The reload count Test.reload_count reads after the client's watcher reloaded a file; a dedicated server reloads no mod file.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugQuad: Rotates model geometry while a model is built for drawing; a dedicated server builds none.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugScreenshots: Compares a captured frame with its reference; a dedicated server draws no frame to capture.
